identity.name: Cossack Hetmanate
native_names: Військо Запорозьке (Viisko Zaporozke, the Zaporozhian Host)

minus.text: Sloboda Ukraine, which 'never became part of the Hetmanate'

land.text: the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships, 'Cossack-held' after the Khmelnytsky Uprising (Zboriv, August 1649)

predecessors.note: The Hetmanate rose from the uprising of 1648 on the Dnieper; the Commonwealth's Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships became de jure autonomous by the Treaty of Zboriv. The Zaporozhian Sich (zaporozhian-cossacks) was the base of the rising and stays a separate dossier.

capitals.name: Chyhyryn
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Chyhyryn (1649-1676)'; the text says the capital moved to Baturyn in 1669, so the dossier ends Chyhyryn in 1668 (Doroshenko's own seat to 1676).

capitals.name: Baturyn
capitals.note: Text: 'in 1669 the capital was transferred to Baturyn'; infobox gives Baturyn from 1663. Destroyed in November 1708.

capitals.name: Hlukhiv
capitals.note: 'Following the destruction of Baturyn, the Hetmanate's capital was moved to Hlukhiv.'

rulers.name: Bohdan Khmelnytsky
rulers.note: Died in Chyhyryn on 6 August 1657 (Khmelnytsky Uprising page).

rulers.name: Ivan Vyhovsky
rulers.note: Elected 1657; deposed at a Black Council in September 1659.

rulers.name: Yurii Khmelnytsky
rulers.note: Elected 1659 aged 18; 'in January 1663 Yurii surrendered his hetman's mace' (Ruin page) but 'held on to the right bank'.

rulers.name: Petro Doroshenko
rulers.title: right-bank hetman 1665, sole hetman from 8 June 1668
rulers.note: Accepted Ottoman protection in 1669; capitulated in 1676.

rulers.name: Demian Mnohohrishny
rulers.title: left-bank hetman
rulers.note: Proclaimed 1669; the end year is the year Samoilovych was elected (the page gives no deposition date).

rulers.name: Ivan Samoilovych
rulers.note: Elected 1672; his removal in 1687 ends the Ruin (Ruin page: 25 July 1687).

rulers.name: Ivan Mazepa
rulers.note: Allied with the Swedes on 28 October 1708; died in Bender 2 October 1709.

rulers.name: Ivan Skoropadsky
rulers.note: Appointed 17 November 1708; end year bridged from the 1722 acting hetman (the page gives no death year).

rulers.name: Pavlo Polubotok
rulers.title: acting hetman
rulers.note: Died in prison in December 1724. Pylyp Orlyk, elected in April 1710, ruled only in exile and is not listed.

rulers.name: Danylo Apostol
rulers.note: Elected 1 October 1727; died 1734 ('After Apostol's death in 1734, power in the Hetmanate was transferred' to the Governing Council of the Hetman Office); no hetman until Razumovsky (1750). End year corrected by reviewer eu-16-x.

rulers.name: Governing Council of the Hetman Office (no hetman)
rulers.note: 'After Apostol's death in 1734, power in the Hetmanate was transferred to the Governing Council of the Hetman Office' (six members, three Russian army officers and three Cossack representatives; 'The real power belonged to the head of the former group'); 'in 1747 a special decree reinstated the position of hetman', but no hetman is named until Kyrylo Rozumovsky was 'elected' in March 1750.

correction.text: the Dnieper Cossack towns round Korsun and Chyhyryn where the rising of 1648 was fought, with the Sich as its base

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the year of the rising. The page dates the first fights (Tomakivka 25 January, Zhovti Vody 29 April, Korsun 25 May 1648); the Cherkasy oblast core is my reading. The boundary is not on any page.

correction.text: the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships, 16 districts on both banks (1649)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 312,000 km2 for 1649-1667; this region resolves to about 226,000 km2 (895 cells, ratio 0.73). An earlier draft used the gazetteer region 'Chernigov', which resolves to the Chernihiv, Bryansk and Kursk oblasts and so drew the Hetmanate over all of Kursk and Bryansk oblasts, which were Muscovite (reviewer's gazetteer trace, 2026-11-01); it is replaced by Chernihiv oblast plus a 60 km disk round Starodub. The lead of the Hetmanate page puts territory 'in parts of Belarus and southwestern Russia' (the second phrase linked to the Starodub Regiment) and the Treaty of Perpetual Peace page lists 'Chernigov, Starodub' among the cities ceded to Russia, so both lay in the Commonwealth before; no page opened dates the Starodub regiment, so the disk is a confidence-2 reading before 1654. Sumy oblast is drawn without Cliopatria's Sloboda Ukraine (1700 shape), because the Hetmanate page says that region 'never became part of the Hetmanate'; Cliopatria's shape starts in 1670, so for 1649-1669 this is an approximation. The shape is still below the infobox figure and the page gives no method for 312,000 km2; Kursk and Bryansk oblasts are not restored to close the gap. Zboriv (19 August 1649) 'provided autonomy to Cossack-held voivodeships of Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv'. The Khmelnytsky Uprising page says Bila Tserkva (1651) limited autonomy to the Kyiv voivodeship, but the Hetmanate infobox keeps 312,000 km2 to 1667 and the Hetmanate kept the ground, so the shape is not cut in 1651. From January 1654 the Hetmanate is a Russian protectorate (the Tsardom dossier carries the vassal_start); from 1663 two hetmans share the land (Yurii Khmelnytsky on the right bank).

Region: Chernihiv oblast, a 60 km disk round Starodub, Poltava, Sumy without Sloboda Ukraine, Kyiv city and a 60 km disk round Pereyaslav (about 104,000 km2, 411 cells); Kursk and Bryansk oblasts are not part of it.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On 9 June 1668 Doroshenko proclaimed himself hetman of a united Ukraine' (Ruin page; the Hetmanate page says 8 June). It is a claim on both banks, not a documented administration: from 1669 the left bank has its own hetman, Mnohohrishny, under Russia, so the right bank here is a confidence-2 reading. The infobox status says '1668-1669: de facto independent'. The both-banks region resolves to about 226,000 km2 (895 cells) once Kursk and Bryansk oblasts are removed (see the 1649 keyframe).

correction.text: both banks as in 1668-1671: the left bank under Samoilovych, the right bank in the Hetmanate's shape as an Ottoman protectorate (infobox 1669-1685) and occupation (1672-)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, replacing an earlier draft that dropped the right bank in 1672 without any loss event. The Hetmanate page's infobox gives the Right Bank as a 'protectorate of the Ottoman Empire' for 1669-1685; the text says right-bank Ukraine 'was temporarily occupied by the Ottoman Empire in the period of 1672-1699', that in 1672 'Ottoman troops captured Podillia, the Bratslav region, and the southern Kyiv region', and that Doroshenko 'capitulated, surrendering the hetman's capital of Chyhyryn' in 1676. I found no right-bank hetman named after Doroshenko's 1676 capitulation on the pages opened, and the page describes the 1681 Bakhchysarai peace as leaving the Dnieper-Buh land uninhabited for twenty years, so the right bank here is a confidence-2 reading: it stays in the Hetmanate's shape, hatched by the Ottoman occupation of the ledger, until the Treaty of Perpetual Peace (6 May 1686) divides the Hetmanate and the ledger records the loss to the Commonwealth. Area: about 226,000 km2 (895 cells), no infobox figure for these years.

correction.text: left-bank Ukraine including Kyiv, 'the Hetmanate' of 1686-1764

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 208,000 km2 for 1686-1764; the left-bank region resolves to about 104,000 km2 (411 cells, ratio 0.50), so it is drawn at about half of the infobox figure. The page gives no method for 208,000 km2. The drawn shape is Chernihiv, Poltava and Sumy oblasts (the last without Cliopatria's Sloboda Ukraine, which 'never became part of the Hetmanate'), Kyiv city and 60 km disks round Pereyaslav and Starodub; it leaves out Kursk and Bryansk oblasts (Muscovite land that an earlier draft drew by mistake through the region 'Chernigov', which gave 174,000 km2), the Zaporozhian Sich lands (a separate Host, 'nominally dependent both on the hetman and the tsar'), and the Belarusian and Russian lands named in the lead, of which only the Starodub regiment is drawn. I take the drawn shape as the better statement of what the pages place in the Hetmanate and have not enlarged it to meet the infobox. The right bank leaves the shape in 1686: the Treaty of Perpetual Peace (6 May 1686) 'secured Russia's possession of left-bank Ukraine, plus the right-bank city of Kiev' while 'Poland retained right-bank Ukraine' (Treaty page), and in 1699 'the Poles abolished the Cossack self-government and the regimental system' on the right bank (Hetmanate page). After Poltava (8 July 1709) 'the Hetmanate's autonomy became nominal', yet the shape runs to the 1764 liquidation.

'The Hetmanate existed between 1648 and 1764, although its administrative-judicial system persisted until 1781.' The Khmelnytsky Uprising page opens the rising on 25 January 1648; the page gives no founding day.

ledger.note: 19 August 1649: Zboriv gives the Cossacks the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships. 'The treaty provided autonomy to Cossack-held voivodeships of Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv.' Autonomy under the crown (de jure part of the Commonwealth: Hetmanate page), so the gain is the Hetmanate's own territory. Khmelnytsky had entered Kyiv on 2 January 1649.

region.text: Konotop and the Sula-Seim left bank where Vyhovsky fought Russia in 1658-1659

ledger.note: September 1658: Vyhovsky turns to Poland. He 'allied himself with the Poles' in September 1658 (Hadiach, 16 September per the Hetmanate page) and in 1659, with Tatar support, beat the Russians at Konotop; the Left Bank stayed with Russia's Cossack faction.
September 1659: Vyhovsky falls. He was deposed at a Black Council in September 1659 (Hetmanate page), and a new Treaty of Pereiaslav with Russia was concluded that year (Russo-Polish War page).

ledger.note: Late 1663: the Polish king invades the left bank. the Polish-Lithuanian king crossed the Dnieper and invaded left-bank Ukraine in late 1663 (page); the siege of Hlukhiv failed in January 1664. Right-bank Ukraine under Yurii Khmelnytsky is the other half: the Hetmanate is partitioned in January 1663 (Ruin page).

'On 9 June 1668 Doroshenko proclaimed himself hetman of a united Ukraine' (the Hetmanate page lists him as sole hetman from 8 June 1668); in 1669 he 'accepted the protection of the Ottoman sultan near Korsun'. The page does not say the Commonwealth ceded the right bank; the gain is the claim made good, confidence 2.

region.text: Podillia, the Bratslav region and the southern Kyiv region; the right bank

ledger.note: 1672: the Ottomans take the right bank. 'In 1672, Ottoman troops captured Podillia, the Bratslav region, and the southern Kyiv region'; the right bank was 'temporarily occupied by the Ottoman Empire in the period of 1672-1699', and the infobox gives it as a 'protectorate of the Ottoman Empire' for 1669-1685. Hatched from the Hetmanate's side (counterpart = occupier) from 1672 until the 1686 division, when the right bank leaves the Hetmanate by the loss below; Podolia proper was Commonwealth land and belongs to its dossier. Doroshenko 'capitulated, surrendering the hetman's capital of Chyhyryn' in 1676 (the shape keeps the right bank to 1685, confidence 2).

region.text: the Army of Lower Zaporozhia, 'nominally dependent both on the hetman and the tsar'

ledger.note: 6 May 1686: the Eternal Peace leaves the Sich 'nominally dependent both on the hetman and the tsar'. The treaty (Treaty of Perpetual Peace page, signed in Moscow 6 May 1686) divides Ukraine between Russia (left bank plus Kyiv) and the Commonwealth (right bank) and cedes 'the region of Zaporizhian Sich' to Russia; the Hetmanate's claim is nominal.

region.text: right-bank Ukraine, which the Treaty of Perpetual Peace left to the Commonwealth

ledger.note: 6 May 1686: the Treaty of Perpetual Peace ('signed in Moscow on 6 May 1686') 'secured Russia's possession of left-bank Ukraine, plus the right-bank city of Kiev', and 'Poland retained right-bank Ukraine' (Treaty page); the Hetmanate page says the treaty 'established the division of the Hetmanate'. On the right bank 'the Poles abolished the Cossack self-government and the regimental system in 1699' (Hetmanate page), so the Hetmanate is left-bank only from this year. Confidence 2: the page gives the Ottoman occupation of the right bank as running to 1699, and the Commonwealth dossier records no 1686 gain from the Hetmanate (only the 1699 gain of Podolia from the Ottomans).

ledger.note: 13 November 1708: Russia strikes the Hetmanate. After Mazepa allied with the Swedes (28 October 1708), Muscovite troops sacked Baturyn on 13 November (Hetmanate page's dated list).
November 1708: the capital moves to Hlukhiv. 'Following the destruction of Baturyn, the Hetmanate's capital was moved to Hlukhiv' (infobox 1708-1764); Skoropadsky was appointed on 17 November 1708.

May 1709: the Sich is destroyed. It joined Mazepa's alliance in March 1709; Peter I ordered its destruction and his troops executed thousands in May 1709 (page, paraphrased), ending the nominal hetman's supremacy over it.

ledger.note: 8 July 1709: Poltava ends Mazepa's revolt. 'The decisive battle of Poltava, which took place on 8 July 1709 ended in the defeat of Swedish forces'; 'the Hetmanate's autonomy became nominal and the Governorate of Kyiv was established.'

region.text: the Hetmanate's left-bank land, 'incorporated as the Little Russia Governorate' 1764-1781

ledger.note: 21 October 1764: the left-bank land passes to Russia on the decree, not from 1721. "According to a decree issued on 21 October 1764, the hetman's post was officially liquidated"; "from 1764 to 1781, the Cossack Hetmanate was incorporated as the Little Russia Governorate headed by Pyotr Rumyantsev". Before that the page has the Hetmanate as an autonomous protectorate: "After 1654: Protectorate of the Tsardom of Moscow and Russian Empire" (infobox); "the Zaporozhian Host became an autonomous Hetmanate within the Russian state" (1654); "After the Battle of Poltava, the Hetmanate's autonomy became nominal" (1709). Request R086: russian-empire is no longer listed in identity.successors, because the handover has no date and rule R2 gave the Russian Empire every conflict cell on the left bank from 1721; this loss hands the land over on the date instead, and hierarchy.csv draws the Hetmanate inside the Russian Empire as a vassal to 1764.

region.text: the Hetmanate's left-bank land, 'incorporated as the Little Russia Governorate' 1764-1781

ledger.note: 21 October 1764: Catherine II abolishes the hetmanate. 'According to a decree issued on 21 October 1764, the hetman's post was officially liquidated'; the land becomes the Little Russia Governorate to 1781, when 'regimental division of the Hetmanate was abolished' (27 September). The infobox gives the abolition as '21 (10) November 1764' against 'a decree issued on 21 October 1764' in the text; the page does not reconcile them, and the dossier takes October (the text).

certainty.note: The Hetmanate was a de facto frontier state on the steppe edge; only the voivodeship names of Zboriv define it, with no surveyed line.
The Dnieper line against the Commonwealth is treaty-fixed by Andrusovo (1667) and the Eternal Peace (1686) but the Russian, Sloboda and steppe limits are not.

notes:
New state: Cliopatria has no Cossack Hetmanate row. The slug cossack-hetmanate was asked for by eu-16-h (tsardom-of-russia counterpart of its 1654 vassal_start) and eu-16-i. Wikidata id not known (wikidata.org unreachable), left null. Overlaps and conflicts to settle: (1) zaporozhian-cossacks (Cliopatria, 1552-1775) is the Host proper, 'its official name was the Zaporozhian Host' per the Hetmanate page, so the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth ledger's 1649-1654 vassal events name zaporozhian-cossacks where this dossier is the counterpart; reviewers should decide whether those events point here. (2) The Commonwealth dossier narrows the autonomy to Kiev+Cherkasy in 1651-1653 (Bila Tserkva); this dossier keeps the Zboriv extent because the Hetmanate page's infobox keeps 312,000 km2 to 1667. (3) The tsardom-of-russia vassal_start (1654, cossack-hetmanate) has no vassal_end: 1764 (or 1709 for the nominal autonomy) belongs in that dossier or in russian-empire; the vassal tint cannot be written from this side (the schema puts it in the suzerain's ledger). (4) The pages differ on Zboriv (18 vs 19 August 1649), Pereyaslav (January vs March 1654), Doroshenko (8 vs 9 June 1668), Baturyn as capital (1663 vs 1669), Khmelnytsky's entry into Kyiv (Christmas 1648 vs 2 January 1649). (5) The Hetmanate page says the administrative system lasted to 1781; the dossier ends at 1764 (the infobox and the decree). Not opened (page budget): Treaty of Zboriv, Treaty of Hadiach, Pereyaslav Agreement, Polish-Ottoman War (1672-1676), Treaty of Karlowitz (the right bank returned to Poland in 1699), Great Northern War, Zaporozhian Sich; their dates here come from the five pages listed. Right bank: it leaves the Hetmanate by a loss event in 1686 (Treaty of Perpetual Peace, to the Commonwealth), after a keyframe 1672-1685 that keeps it under the Ottoman occupation/protectorate (Hetmanate infobox: right bank 'protectorate of the Ottoman Empire' 1669-1685); on the right bank 'the Poles abolished the Cossack self-government and the regimental system in 1699' (Hetmanate page). The Ottoman occupation event is written from the Hetmanate's side with the occupier as counterpart, as the Tang worked example does, and ends in 1686 with the division. Repairs of 2026-11-01 after the review: the region 'Chernigov' (which resolves to the Chernihiv, Bryansk and Kursk oblasts) is replaced everywhere by Chernihiv oblast plus a 60 km disk round Starodub, and Sumy oblast is drawn without Cliopatria's Sloboda Ukraine; the drawn areas are about 226,000 km2 for both banks (infobox 312,000, ratio 0.73) and about 104,000 km2 for the left bank (infobox 208,000, ratio 0.50), explained in the keyframe notes. The Ottoman (me-10) and Commonwealth (eu-15) dossiers do not carry the matching events (an Ottoman protectorate over the right bank 1669-1685 and a 1686 gain of the right bank from the Hetmanate); see the batch notes.
R086 (3 Nov 2026): russian-empire removed from identity.successors (the entry read: the left bank, 'From 1764 to 1781, the Cossack Hetmanate was incorporated as the Little Russia Governorate'). A handover has no date and rule R2 applied it from the Russian Empire's start (1721), drawing the left bank as direct Russian land for 1721-1763. The handover is now the loss at 1764-10 (ledger/19) before the dissolve.
